blocks.text: Ioh. XIII, 12. etc. up to ch. XVIII.
Ioh. XVIII, 24. Matth. XXVI, 57. Marc. XIV, 53. Luc. XXII, 54.

It is recorded in the Talmudic tractate Bava Kama, ch. 7, last section, that it was forbidden by law to raise cocks in Jerusalem: אין מגדלין תרנגולין בירושלם מפני קדושים, They do not raise [II, 693] cocks in Jerusalem on account of the holy things, nor do the priests raise them anywhere in the land of Israel. The Gloss gives the reason: Israelites too are forbidden to raise cocks in Jerusalem on account of the holy things; for the Israelites ate there the flesh of the peace offerings and thank offerings, and it is the habit of cocks to turn over dunghills, and from them they might perhaps bring out the flesh of creeping things, by which those holy things that were to be eaten could be defiled. Hence some interpreters have come to doubt the cockcrow mentioned by the writers of the Gospels. For my part, I would count that Talmudic rule among the fictitious prohibitions which the petty subtlety of the Jewish masters drew out of the simple laws of Moses, but which no one heeded outside the shade of the schools. Certainly, if one wishes to argue the matter from the Talmud, many more passages from the same Talmud can be set against that passage of Bava Kama in which cocks and cockcrow are mentioned, some of which Bochart has cited above. And in the tractate Berachoth we read of a cock that, because it had pierced an infant's skull at the spot where it is most tender and killed the infant, was punished by stoning by sentence of the Sanhedrin. See Buxtorf, Lexic. Chald. p. 2654. But if anyone is unwilling to accept this, let him follow the opinion of Reland (in the oration de Galli cantu Hierosolymis audito, Rotterdam 1709, 8vo), that Pilate, or the other Romans living in the city, being either wholly indifferent to or ignorant of Jewish institutions, kept cocks or hens, either for food or for the sake of auspices. For the opinions of others, listed and assessed, see Wolf, Curae Philologg. on Matth. XXVI, 34, vol. 1, p. 378 ff. One may also compare Michaelis, Einleit. in das N. T. vol. 1, p. 71. 72.
